To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the features that have the highest predictive power are the head noun (the most common feature), the gender and number of the head noun, and the number of mentions.

(i) the most important features are the ones that indicate that the candidate mentions have the same head noun and the same NP type; (ii) the most important interactions are the ones between features that indicate that the mentions are the same head noun, the same NP type, and have the same gender; (iii) the most useful features for coreference resolution are the ones that have a low entropy; (iv) the most useful interactions are the ones that include features that have a high entropy;

(i) features are not equally important, (ii) the combination of the most informative features yields a significant improvement in accuracy, (iii) there are no clear patterns of feature interaction, (iv) sample selection is a relevant factor, (v) there are no significant differences in the importance of the features between the two languages, and (vi) there is no clear correlation between the importance of a feature and its informativeness.
